:::caution[Not released yet]
HotLoop for CODESYS is built and has run against a real CODESYS runtime in the lab, and it is not out. It needs HotLoop 4.19.0, and the chart and the provisioner image are not published, so you can't install it yet. [Where it stands](/codesys/where-it-stands/) has the list.
:::

This is the list of what is done and what is left, in the order it gets done. It promises nothing that isn't in the code or in a test plan, and it is mostly [the not-proven list](/codesys/where-it-stands/) turned into work.

## Built

- [x] A chart around HotLoop Edge with defaults for a runtime on a node: SQLite, one replica, tolerations that keep both pods through a lost control plane.
- [x] A provisioner that applies a profile and keeps it right, with a revision that protects what a person changed.
- [x] The device, tags, alarm, and screen made with no hand step, against a CODESYS Control for Linux SL 4.22.0.0 runtime in a container.
- [x] Recovery from a runtime restart with no hands, about 88 seconds in the lab.
- [x] A signed sign-in from the EmberCORE dashboard, with the refusals.

## To ship the first version

- [ ] HotLoop 4.19.0 released.
- [ ] The chart published at `https://hotloop.io/hotloop-codesys/`.
- [ ] The provisioner image public, so it pulls with no login.
- [ ] Release notes for the first version.

## To prove

- [ ] An install from the real App Store page, as staff do it.
- [ ] A physical controller.
- [ ] k3s v1.35.7.
- [ ] A node that really loses its link to the control plane, with the pods kept.
- [ ] A download from the CODESYS IDE while the runtime stays up.
- [ ] A runtime on the host's own network beside the HotLoop pod on one node.
- [ ] A runtime with user management on, and a certificate-secured OPC UA endpoint.

Nothing past this list is decided yet. When it is, it goes here with the same marks: built, or not built.
